Chemist-confirmed O2 feed at 2 equiv; equivalents and MFC flow are defined at inlet/STP.

chemistry_plan.mixing_order_reasoning: All Stage 1 reagents (substrate 1, acrylonitrile, Ir photocatalyst) are co-dissolved in degassed EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1) and loaded as a single stream. No incompatibility between these species pre-irradiation. O₂ is introduced only at Stage 2 inlet via T-mixer joining Stage 1 effluent with gas stream, creating gas-liquid segmented flow.
chemistry_plan.deoxygenation_reasoning: Stage 1 Giese reaction proceeds via carbon radical intermediates that are quenched by O₂. Batch protocol specifies argon atmosphere and degassed solvent. In flow: (1) pre-sparge stock solution with Ar before loading, (2) use gas-tight syringe or sealed reservoir, (3) install check valve (CV-3301) between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 O₂ introduction point to prevent backflow. Inline degasser unavailable per inventory.
chemistry_plan.quench_reasoning: No quench step described in the batch protocol between or after stages. The reaction mixture is simply collected after Stage 2.
chemistry_plan.batch_limitations_reasoning: mass_transfer_gas_liquid: matched [gas-liquid mass transfer]; photon_penetration: matched [photon delivery, photon flux]; stirring_diffusion: matched [stirring]
chemistry_plan.wavelength_reasoning: Target wavelength fixed by the standardized intake package.
chemistry_plan.confidence_notes: Stage 2 oxidation mechanism (singlet O₂ vs superoxide pathway) is a hypothesis — the protocol only states O₂ as terminal oxidant under irradiation. The 2.0 equiv O₂ is a chemist-specified screening starting point, not a measured stoichiometric requirement. Gas backflow was observed in prior KHU experiment at 0.43 mL/min O₂ / 0.02 mL/min liquid; the check valve (CV-3301, 1 bar cracking pressure) and appropriate BPR selection are critical engineering mitigations but have not been validated. Rate-limiting step designation is avoided since no kinetic data exists — the hypothesis is that photon delivery limits both stages. The UV-150 can only be shared between stages if run sequentially (two separate runs) or if two UV-150 modules at 450 nm exist (inventory shows only one UV-150 slot); alternative for one stage is Manual 1 or Manual 2 strip LED at 448 nm. This is an important hardware constraint for continuous two-stage operation.

batch_record.raw_text:
Step 1: Giese reaction
A re-sealable pressure tube (13 × 100 mm) equipped with a magnetic stir bar was charged with (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv), acrylonitrile (2, 0.4 mmol, 2.0 equiv), and [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.001 mmol, 0.5 mol %) under an argon atmosphere. A degassed solvent mixture (2.0 mL, 0.1 M with respect to 1) of EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1, v/v) was added, and the resulting light greenish-yellow mixture, under vigorous magnetic stirring, was positioned 3 cm from a pair of 5 W blue LEDs (λmax = 452 nm) and irradiated at room temperature (25 °C, maintained with a cooling fan to counteract heating from the LEDs) for 4 h 

Step 2: Oxidation reaction
After 4 h, the cap of the tube was removed to expose the reaction mixture to ambient air, providing atmospheric oxygen as the terminal oxidant, and stirring was continued under otherwise identical irradiation conditions for an additional 6 h.

intake_package.raw_protocol:
Step 1: Giese reaction
A re-sealable pressure tube (13 × 100 mm) equipped with a magnetic stir bar was charged with (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv), acrylonitrile (2, 0.4 mmol, 2.0 equiv), and [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.001 mmol, 0.5 mol %) under an argon atmosphere. A degassed solvent mixture (2.0 mL, 0.1 M with respect to 1) of EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1, v/v) was added, and the resulting light greenish-yellow mixture, under vigorous magnetic stirring, was positioned 3 cm from a pair of 5 W blue LEDs (λmax = 452 nm) and irradiated at room temperature (25 °C, maintained with a cooling fan to counteract heating from the LEDs) for 4 h 

Step 2: Oxidation reaction
After 4 h, the cap of the tube was removed to expose the reaction mixture to ambient air, providing atmospheric oxygen as the terminal oxidant, and stirring was continued under otherwise identical irradiation conditions for an additional 6 h.

intake_package.objective: Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage flow process that maximizes the final yield of sulfoxide 4a while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.
intake_package.historical_data: Qualitative KHU observation reported on 15 September 2026: liquid solution flow was 0.02 mL/min and the gas actually used was pure oxygen at a reported 0.43 mL/min. Gas reverse flow toward Stage 1 was observed. The earlier design had specified air, but the experiment used oxygen instead. The reference conditions of that reported experimental gas reading were not independently verified. No yield, gas supply pressure, startup sequence, or pressure traces were supplied. This is qualitative operability evidence, not a kinetic data point or a calibrated backflow model. Reducing gas flow alone does not prove that reverse flow is prevented. Stage 1 must remain oxygen-free.

hypotheses: Stage 1 performance may depend on effective oxygen exclusion and photon delivery. Incomplete sulfide formation will limit the material available for subsequent oxidation. Stage 2 may depend on oxygen availability and gas–liquid transport. Use the batch reaction time as a reference rather than a fixed target, and determine the residence time based on flow performance. Balance photon delivery, oxygen feed, pressure, and stage-specific residence times based on the final sulfoxide yield and selectivity.

operating_limits.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
operating_limits.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
operating_limits.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.
catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
operating_limits.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
operating_constraints.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

multistep.stage_definition:
Step 1: Giese reaction
A re-sealable pressure tube (13 × 100 mm) equipped with a magnetic stir bar was charged with (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv), acrylonitrile (2, 0.4 mmol, 2.0 equiv), and [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.001 mmol, 0.5 mol %) under an argon atmosphere. A degassed solvent mixture (2.0 mL, 0.1 M with respect to 1) of EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1, v/v) was added, and the resulting light greenish-yellow mixture, under vigorous magnetic stirring, was positioned 3 cm from a pair of 5 W blue LEDs (λmax = 452 nm) and irradiated at room temperature (25 °C, maintained with a cooling fan to counteract heating from the LEDs) for 4 h 

Step 2: Oxidation reaction
After 4 h, the cap of the tube was removed to expose the reaction mixture to ambient air, providing atmospheric oxygen as the terminal oxidant, and stirring was continued under otherwise identical irradiation conditions for an additional 6 h.

question_log.question: Please provide or confirm the batch reaction protocol, including substrate, product, solvent, concentration, scale, reagents, equivalents, catalyst/additives, gas atmosphere, temperature, time, irradiation/light source if any, and reported yield.
question_log.why_needed: The design pipeline needs protocol facts before translation.

question_log.question: What is the main goal for the first flow design? Examples: first safe screening design, reproduce batch yield, improve throughput, maximize conversion, minimize residence time, or test a specific hypothesis.
question_log.why_needed: The council ranks candidate designs against this objective.

question_log.question: Please confirm the intended reaction transformation. State the transformation family and, where known, the substrate, product, bond formed, and bond broken.
question_log.expected_format: Short text such as 'hydrogenolysis/debenzylation of A to B; C-N protecting-group bond broken'.
question_log.why_needed: A model-only chemistry identity cannot authorize an executable design.

question_log.question: Do you have historical experimental data or previous flow attempts for this reaction? If yes, provide a table with conditions and results.
question_log.expected_format: Table/CSV/text with entry, T, concentration, pressure, flows, residence times, reactor volume, tubing ID, product/yield/conversion/selectivity, and notes; or mark unavailable.
question_log.why_needed: Measured evidence has highest design authority.

question_log.question: Do you have inventory constraints that the design must use? Provide available reactor volumes, tubing IDs/materials, pumps, pressure/BPR options, gas MFC limits, light sources, and temperature ranges.
question_log.expected_format: LabInventory JSON preferred; free text accepted; or mark unavailable.
question_log.why_needed: Hard hardware constraints must be enforced before final design.

question_log.question: Are there operating limits that must not be exceeded? Examples: max pressure, max temperature, max/min flow rate, max residence time, forbidden solvents, gas safety limits, oxygen limits, or material compatibility limits.
question_log.expected_format: Free text or JSON; or mark unavailable.
question_log.why_needed: Safety and operating limits constrain feasible candidates.

question_log.question: Do you have chemical or engineering hypotheses the agent should consider? Examples: oxygen mass-transfer limitation, photon limitation, slow kinetics, degradation, gas-liquid ratio, residence-time sensitivity, or light intensity importance.
question_log.expected_format: Bullet list/free text; or mark unavailable.
question_log.why_needed: Hypotheses guide experiment design but are not treated as facts.

question_log.question: How many molar equivalents of active reagent gas should be delivered relative to the limiting substrate? FlowPilot will calculate this from the inlet/STP MFC flow, not the compressed in-channel flow.
question_log.expected_format: Positive number in equivalents, for example: 2.0 equiv.
question_log.why_needed: A target equivalent is required for stoichiometric inlet/STP gas-flow closure.
question_log.decision_impact: Directly changes the inlet/STP MFC setpoint and both reported apparent residence times.

question_log.question: At which reaction stage is the reagent gas first introduced? Identify the stage number or describe the stage operation.
question_log.expected_format: Stage number and short description, for example: Stage 2, aerobic oxidation.
question_log.why_needed: The gas feed must be attached to exactly one stage in a multistep topology.
question_log.decision_impact: Determines the mixer, MFC connection, stage temperature, and stage residence-time calculation.

answers.answer: Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage flow process that maximizes the final yield of sulfoxide 4a while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.

Stage 1 performance may depend on effective oxygen exclusion and photon delivery. Incomplete sulfide formation will limit the material available for subsequent oxidation. Stage 2 may depend on oxygen availability and gas–liquid transport. Use the batch reaction time as a reference rather than a fixed target, and determine the residence time based on flow performance. Balance photon delivery, oxygen feed, pressure, and stage-specific residence times based on the final sulfoxide yield and selectivity.
Use at least 2.0 equiv of oxygen relative to the limiting substrate; higher oxygen equivalents may be used if justified by the reaction and operating conditions.
Introduce oxygen only at the Stage 2 inlet. Stage 1 must remain oxygen-free.
Pure oxygen (O2), 100 mol% O2. Require pure oxygen at Stage 2; do not use air.

Qualitative KHU observation reported on 15 September 2026: liquid solution flow was 0.02 mL/min and the gas actually used was pure oxygen at a reported 0.43 mL/min. Gas reverse flow toward Stage 1 was observed. The earlier design had specified air, but the experiment used oxygen instead. The reference conditions of that reported experimental gas reading were not independently verified. No yield, gas supply pressure, startup sequence, or pressure traces were supplied. This is qualitative operability evidence, not a kinetic data point or a calibrated backflow model. Reducing gas flow alone does not prove that reverse flow is prevented. Stage 1 must remain oxygen-free.

answer.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
answer.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
answer.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.
catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
answer.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

### Design objective
Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage flow process that maximizes the final yield of sulfoxide 4a while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.

Screening priority selection: auto

### Measured evidence / historical data
Qualitative KHU observation reported on 15 September 2026: liquid solution flow was 0.02 mL/min and the gas actually used was pure oxygen at a reported 0.43 mL/min. Gas reverse flow toward Stage 1 was observed. The earlier design had specified air, but the experiment used oxygen instead. The reference conditions of that reported experimental gas reading were not independently verified. No yield, gas supply pressure, startup sequence, or pressure traces were supplied. This is qualitative operability evidence, not a kinetic data point or a calibrated backflow model. Reducing gas flow alone does not prove that reverse flow is prevented. Stage 1 must remain oxygen-free.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: photoredox radical addition + oxidation, fac-[Ir(ppy)3], MiChS photoreactor, 2 mm quartz, 2.7 mL, 30 min residence, 0.09 mL/min, 425 nm — similar Ir-photoredox mechanism, different catalyst and reactor; supports short residence times (30 min) vs 24 h batch; adjusted: our UV-150 with 10 mL coil and different Ir catalyst, use 20 min as starting screen (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling, FEP 10 mL, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min, 440 nm, 50°C, 34 W — same photocatalyst family (dF(CF3)ppy ligand), different coupling type and temperature; adjusted: at 25°C use longer 20 min, 0.50 mL/min in 10 mL PFA UV-150 coil (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 3: Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 photoredox/Ni dual catalysis, Vapourtec E-series UV-150, 10 mL, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm, 30°C — closest match: same UV-150 reactor, same 450 nm wavelength, same Ir catalyst class; key difference: dual catalysis vs single photocatalyst; adjusted: use 0.50 mL/min (20 min) as more aggressive screen since single-catalyst radical addition may be faster than dual-catalysis cross-coupling (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling, FEP 10 mL, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min, 440 nm, 50°C, 34 W — same photocatalyst family (dF(CF3)ppy ligand), different coupling type and temperature; adjusted: at 25°C use longer 20 min, 0.50 mL/min in 10 mL PFA UV-150 coil (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 3: Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 photoredox/Ni dual catalysis, Vapourtec E-series UV-150, 10 mL, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm, 30°C — closest match: same UV-150 reactor, same 450 nm wavelength, same Ir catalyst class; key difference: dual catalysis vs single photocatalyst; adjusted: use 0.50 mL/min (20 min) as more aggressive screen since single-catalyst radical addition may be faster than dual-catalysis cross-coupling (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: photoredox radical addition + oxidation, fac-[Ir(ppy)3], MiChS photoreactor, 2 mm quartz, 2.7 mL, 30 min residence, 0.09 mL/min, 425 nm — similar Ir-photoredox mechanism, different catalyst and reactor; supports short residence times (30 min) vs 24 h batch; adjusted: our UV-150 with 10 mL coil and different Ir catalyst, use 20 min as starting screen (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling, FEP 10 mL, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min, 440 nm, 50°C, 34 W — same photocatalyst family (dF(CF3)ppy ligand), different coupling type and temperature; adjusted: at 25°C use longer 20 min, 0.50 mL/min in 10 mL PFA UV-150 coil (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 3: Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 photoredox/Ni dual catalysis, Vapourtec E-series UV-150, 10 mL, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm, 30°C — closest match: same UV-150 reactor, same 450 nm wavelength, same Ir catalyst class; key difference: dual catalysis vs single photocatalyst; adjusted: use 0.50 mL/min (20 min) as more aggressive screen since single-catalyst radical addition may be faster than dual-catalysis cross-coupling (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A containing (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 1.0 equiv, 0.1 M), [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.5 mol%, 0.0005 M), acrylonitrile (2, 2.0 equiv, 0.2 M), ethanol, pH 9 aqueous buffer in EtOH:pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v), pre-sparged with Ar at 0.1 M; concentration basis: reference component: (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row3 (2 mL, 1 mm ID, PFA) at 25 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row6 (10 mL, 1 mm ID, FEP) at 25 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:mfc_ffc00.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.02 mL/min.
Set gas Stream B (O2) to 0.09 sccm at inlet/STP (0.012422 mL/min in-channel; 2.0078 equiv supplied).
post_reactor_steps: Collect product stream in vial under ambient conditions. No quench step specified in batch protocol.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
For shutdown, stop reactive cofeeds and reagent gas first, flush with a compatible declared solvent, then depressurize through the controlled outlet.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: photoredox radical addition + oxidation, fac-[Ir(ppy)3], MiChS photoreactor, 2 mm quartz, 2.7 mL, 30 min residence, 0.09 mL/min, 425 nm — similar Ir-photoredox mechanism, different catalyst and reactor; supports short residence times (30 min) vs 24 h batch; adjusted: our UV-150 with 10 mL coil and different Ir catalyst, use 20 min as starting screen (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling, FEP 10 mL, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min, 440 nm, 50°C, 34 W — same photocatalyst family (dF(CF3)ppy ligand), different coupling type and temperature; adjusted: at 25°C use longer 20 min, 0.50 mL/min in 10 mL PFA UV-150 coil (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 3: Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 photoredox/Ni dual catalysis, Vapourtec E-series UV-150, 10 mL, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm, 30°C — closest match: same UV-150 reactor, same 450 nm wavelength, same Ir catalyst class; key difference: dual catalysis vs single photocatalyst; adjusted: use 0.50 mL/min (20 min) as more aggressive screen since single-catalyst radical addition may be faster than dual-catalysis cross-coupling (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

operating_limits.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
operating_limits.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
operating_limits.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.
catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
operating_limits.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved mitigation proposal (requires chemistry, inventory, and O2-service review before adoption): Install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g., CV-3301, service-verified) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction, protecting Stage 1 from reverse gas intrusion. This valve's cracking pressure concerns the pressure difference across it, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Its maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow behaviour must be confirmed before use.

Unapproved mitigation proposal: A pressure-decoupled arrangement (e.g., intermediate collection and re-pressurisation) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is not a designed or approved element and requires full engineering review.

Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.

This valve's cracking pressure concerns the pressure difference across it, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Its maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow behaviour must be confirmed before use.

All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or design is changed by the tool.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

### Measured evidence / historical data
Qualitative KHU observation reported on 15 September 2026: liquid solution flow was 0.02 mL/min and the gas actually used was pure oxygen at a reported 0.43 mL/min. Gas reverse flow toward Stage 1 was observed. The earlier design had specified air, but the experiment used oxygen instead. The reference conditions of that reported experimental gas reading were not independently verified. No yield, gas supply pressure, startup sequence, or pressure traces were supplied. This is qualitative operability evidence, not a kinetic data point or a calibrated backflow model. Reducing gas flow alone does not prove that reverse flow is prevented. Stage 1 must remain oxygen-free.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved mitigation proposal (requires chemistry, inventory, and O2-service review before adoption): Install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g., CV-3301, service-verified) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction, protecting Stage 1 from reverse gas intrusion. This valve's cracking pressure concerns the pressure difference across it, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Its maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow behaviour must be confirmed before use.

Unapproved mitigation proposal: A pressure-decoupled arrangement (e.g., intermediate collection and re-pressurisation) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is not a designed or approved element and requires full engineering review.
Reducing gas flow alone does not resolve the unprotected reverse path on the liquid branch, as confirmed by the measured backflow event in the prior experiment and the topology finding.
limitations: Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters: illustrative viscosity (1.0 mPa·s), gas plenum (0.2 mL), MFC required ΔP (1.0 bar), pump response (1.0 s), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), and multiphase resistance multiplier (3.0). These are not laboratory setpoints.
No reversal predicted in the finite simulation windows does not establish safe operation or exclude backflow under real startup, transient, or off-normal conditions.
Reported metric is predicted liquid displacement from the liquid branch at the junction, not oxygen reaching Stage 1 Reactor.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure; steady-state behaviour was only assessed with the hypothetical liquid check valve configuration, which is unassigned and service-unverified.
The CV-3301 check valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve; its maximum pressure rating is unconfirmed.
Isothermal ideal gas model; slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, reaction, and gas-front dynamics are not modelled.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or design is changed by the tool.
The prior experimental gas reverse flow observation (KHU, 15 Sep 2026) used unverified reference conditions and remains unresolved by these simulations.
BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics, and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
Pure O2 use is a gas-source change from the protocol (air); it is unapproved and requires laboratory review before use.

proposed_alternatives: A dedicated check valve (CV-3301 or equivalent) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction is an unapproved proposal: requires engineering review, inventory confirmation, service verification, and oxygen-compatibility assessment before use.
A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., gravity or pressure-controlled transfer) is an unapproved hypothesis requiring separate engineering and chemistry review.

Pure O2 gas supply in place of the batch air atmosphere is an unapproved gas-source change: requires chemist confirmation, oxygen-service review, and materials compatibility assessment before laboratory use.

CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; the valve on the MFC branch does not protect the liquid branch. Branch-specific protection on the liquid line is a separate unapproved item.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, unmeasured parameters (viscosity, compliance, gas plenum, conductance, pump and MFC response times); results are conditional model outputs, not measured evidence or safety certification.

No liquid displacement predicted in entered-profile scenarios does not establish that backflow cannot occur; the unprotected liquid-branch reverse path (st2_mixer → st1_reactor) is an unresolved credible risk confirmed by the KHU qualitative observation.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 (as-designed, gas-first startup): BPR opening pressure was not reached within the simulated window; steady-state behaviour during full pressurisation is unconfirmed for those as-designed cases.
Predicted quantities are liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches Stage 1 Reactor; actual gas transport through the liquid column is not modelled.
Gas check-valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) governs pressure difference across that valve; it does not set a minimum system pressure margin above which backflow is precluded.
Isothermal ideal-gas model; no slug, dissolution, capillary, multiphase front, or reaction model included.
Finite scenario window; no lifetime, frequency, or reliability assessment is provided.
Hypothetical liquid-branch check valve is not assigned, not service-verified, and not in the approved inventory; zero leakage assumed is an idealisation.
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating not supplied; suitability at 7 bar or 8 bar system pressures requires laboratory verification before use.
All candidates share the same unresolved reverse-path finding (BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor); reducing gas flow does not close this path.
Acrylonitrile is listed as excluded from RED pump tubing; all candidates correctly assign liquid feed to BLUE pump, but solvent-wetted component compatibility beyond pump tubing should be confirmed.

uncertainties: specific uncertainty

proposed_alternatives: conditional mitigation and what remains unconfirmed; empty allowed
limitations: explicit limitations of the simulation and missing measurements

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved mitigation proposal (requires chemistry, inventory, and O2-service review before adoption): Install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g., CV-3301, service-verified) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction, protecting Stage 1 from reverse gas intrusion. This valve's cracking pressure concerns the pressure difference across it, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Its maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow behaviour must be confirmed before use.

Unapproved mitigation proposal: A pressure-decoupled arrangement (e.g., intermediate collection and re-pressurisation) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is not a designed or approved element and requires full engineering review.
Reducing gas flow alone does not resolve the unprotected reverse path on the liquid branch, as confirmed by the measured backflow event in the prior experiment and the topology finding.
limitations: Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters: illustrative viscosity (1.0 mPa·s), gas plenum (0.2 mL), MFC required ΔP (1.0 bar), pump response (1.0 s), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), and multiphase resistance multiplier (3.0). These are not laboratory setpoints.
No reversal predicted in the finite simulation windows does not establish safe operation or exclude backflow under real startup, transient, or off-normal conditions.
Reported metric is predicted liquid displacement from the liquid branch at the junction, not oxygen reaching Stage 1 Reactor.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure; steady-state behaviour was only assessed with the hypothetical liquid check valve configuration, which is unassigned and service-unverified.
The CV-3301 check valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve; its maximum pressure rating is unconfirmed.
Isothermal ideal gas model; slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, reaction, and gas-front dynamics are not modelled.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or design is changed by the tool.
The prior experimental gas reverse flow observation (KHU, 15 Sep 2026) used unverified reference conditions and remains unresolved by these simulations.
BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics, and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
Pure O2 use is a gas-source change from the protocol (air); it is unapproved and requires laboratory review before use.

proposed_alternatives: A dedicated check valve (CV-3301 or equivalent) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction is an unapproved proposal: requires engineering review, inventory confirmation, service verification, and oxygen-compatibility assessment before use.
A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., gravity or pressure-controlled transfer) is an unapproved hypothesis requiring separate engineering and chemistry review.

Pure O2 gas supply in place of the batch air atmosphere is an unapproved gas-source change: requires chemist confirmation, oxygen-service review, and materials compatibility assessment before laboratory use.

CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; the valve on the MFC branch does not protect the liquid branch. Branch-specific protection on the liquid line is a separate unapproved item.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, unmeasured parameters (viscosity, compliance, gas plenum, conductance, pump and MFC response times); results are conditional model outputs, not measured evidence or safety certification.

No liquid displacement predicted in entered-profile scenarios does not establish that backflow cannot occur; the unprotected liquid-branch reverse path (st2_mixer → st1_reactor) is an unresolved credible risk confirmed by the KHU qualitative observation.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 (as-designed, gas-first startup): BPR opening pressure was not reached within the simulated window; steady-state behaviour during full pressurisation is unconfirmed for those as-designed cases.
Predicted quantities are liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches Stage 1 Reactor; actual gas transport through the liquid column is not modelled.
Gas check-valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) governs pressure difference across that valve; it does not set a minimum system pressure margin above which backflow is precluded.
Isothermal ideal-gas model; no slug, dissolution, capillary, multiphase front, or reaction model included.
Finite scenario window; no lifetime, frequency, or reliability assessment is provided.
Hypothetical liquid-branch check valve is not assigned, not service-verified, and not in the approved inventory; zero leakage assumed is an idealisation.
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating not supplied; suitability at 7 bar or 8 bar system pressures requires laboratory verification before use.
All candidates share the same unresolved reverse-path finding (BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor); reducing gas flow does not close this path.
Acrylonitrile is listed as excluded from RED pump tubing; all candidates correctly assign liquid feed to BLUE pump, but solvent-wetted component compatibility beyond pump tubing should be confirmed.

uncertainties: specific uncertainty

proposed_alternatives: conditional mitigation and what remains unconfirmed; empty allowed
limitations: explicit limitations of the simulation and missing measurements

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved mitigation proposal (requires chemistry, inventory, and O2-service review before adoption): Install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g., CV-3301, service-verified) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction, protecting Stage 1 from reverse gas intrusion. This valve's cracking pressure concerns the pressure difference across it, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Its maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow behaviour must be confirmed before use.

Unapproved mitigation proposal: A pressure-decoupled arrangement (e.g., intermediate collection and re-pressurisation) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is not a designed or approved element and requires full engineering review.
Reducing gas flow alone does not resolve the unprotected reverse path on the liquid branch, as confirmed by the measured backflow event in the prior experiment and the topology finding.
limitations: Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters: illustrative viscosity (1.0 mPa·s), gas plenum (0.2 mL), MFC required ΔP (1.0 bar), pump response (1.0 s), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), and multiphase resistance multiplier (3.0). These are not laboratory setpoints.
No reversal predicted in the finite simulation windows does not establish safe operation or exclude backflow under real startup, transient, or off-normal conditions.
Reported metric is predicted liquid displacement from the liquid branch at the junction, not oxygen reaching Stage 1 Reactor.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure; steady-state behaviour was only assessed with the hypothetical liquid check valve configuration, which is unassigned and service-unverified.
The CV-3301 check valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve; its maximum pressure rating is unconfirmed.
Isothermal ideal gas model; slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, reaction, and gas-front dynamics are not modelled.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or design is changed by the tool.
The prior experimental gas reverse flow observation (KHU, 15 Sep 2026) used unverified reference conditions and remains unresolved by these simulations.
BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics, and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
Pure O2 use is a gas-source change from the protocol (air); it is unapproved and requires laboratory review before use.

proposed_alternatives: A dedicated check valve (CV-3301 or equivalent) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction is an unapproved proposal: requires engineering review, inventory confirmation, service verification, and oxygen-compatibility assessment before use.
A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., gravity or pressure-controlled transfer) is an unapproved hypothesis requiring separate engineering and chemistry review.

Pure O2 gas supply in place of the batch air atmosphere is an unapproved gas-source change: requires chemist confirmation, oxygen-service review, and materials compatibility assessment before laboratory use.

CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; the valve on the MFC branch does not protect the liquid branch. Branch-specific protection on the liquid line is a separate unapproved item.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, unmeasured parameters (viscosity, compliance, gas plenum, conductance, pump and MFC response times); results are conditional model outputs, not measured evidence or safety certification.

No liquid displacement predicted in entered-profile scenarios does not establish that backflow cannot occur; the unprotected liquid-branch reverse path (st2_mixer → st1_reactor) is an unresolved credible risk confirmed by the KHU qualitative observation.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 (as-designed, gas-first startup): BPR opening pressure was not reached within the simulated window; steady-state behaviour during full pressurisation is unconfirmed for those as-designed cases.
Predicted quantities are liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches Stage 1 Reactor; actual gas transport through the liquid column is not modelled.
Gas check-valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) governs pressure difference across that valve; it does not set a minimum system pressure margin above which backflow is precluded.
Isothermal ideal-gas model; no slug, dissolution, capillary, multiphase front, or reaction model included.
Finite scenario window; no lifetime, frequency, or reliability assessment is provided.
Hypothetical liquid-branch check valve is not assigned, not service-verified, and not in the approved inventory; zero leakage assumed is an idealisation.
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating not supplied; suitability at 7 bar or 8 bar system pressures requires laboratory verification before use.
All candidates share the same unresolved reverse-path finding (BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor); reducing gas flow does not close this path.
Acrylonitrile is listed as excluded from RED pump tubing; all candidates correctly assign liquid feed to BLUE pump, but solvent-wetted component compatibility beyond pump tubing should be confirmed.

DrChemistry.justification: Baseline: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42× batch) in 2 mL PFA/UV-150 450 nm; Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min (0.51× batch) in 20 mL FEP/Manual2, BPR 7 bar. Balanced stage ratios. Interpretable anchor for comparison. Backflow unresolved (shared); all other checks pass.
uncertainties: Stage 1 at 100 min (0.42× batch) may be inadequate for Giese reaction; uncharacterized.
Stage 2 apparent tau is inlet/STP index only; liquid exposure much longer but unverified.
Backflow: unprotected reverse path to Stage 1 unresolved.
CV-3301 pressure rating unconfirmed.
O2 service and gas-source change unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 identical to C1 (100 min, 0.42×). Stage 2 same reactor (20 mL FEP) and inlet tau (181.8 min) but BPR 2.5 bar; in-channel gas volume larger (0.028 mL/min vs 0.012 mL/min), potentially different gas-liquid contact. Useful BPR comparison to C1. Backflow unresolved (shared).
uncertainties: Lower BPR may increase gas void fraction; gas-liquid mass transfer and slug stability uncharacterized.
Stage 1 adequacy at 100 min uncharacterized.
Backflow: unprotected reverse path unresolved.
CV-3301 rating unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04× batch) in 5 mL ETFE/UV-150; provides near-batch Stage 1 exposure. Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min (0.51×) in 20 mL FEP, BPR 7 bar. Large-bore ETFE in Stage 1 (2.4 mm ID, Re≈0.18) is laminar; photon penetration depth at 2.4 mm bore unverified. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm bore: photon penetration and mixing at Re≈0.18 uncharacterized in UV-150.
Stage 2 apparent tau 0.51× batch; adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min in 20 mL FEP, BPR 1.5 bar. Lowest BPR of the 20 mL FEP group; highest in-channel gas volume fraction (0.040 mL/min). Useful low-BPR comparison point. Stage 1 adequacy and backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: BPR 1.5 bar: largest gas void fraction among FEP 20 mL candidates; slug flow stability uncharacterized.
Stage 1 at 100 min (0.42×) may be insufficient.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, BPR 7 bar. Shortest apparent Stage 2 index in the set. Stage 2 exposure substantially below batch anchor; adequacy is an open question. ETFE large bore in Stage 2 may affect gas distribution.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 0.25× batch may be insufficient for sulfide oxidation; uncharacterized.
ETFE 2.4 mm bore Stage 2: gas-liquid distribution uncharacterized.
Stage 1 at 0.42× may be insufficient.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04×) in 5 mL PFA 1 mm/UV-150; near-batch Stage 1 in a narrow-bore coil with better photon penetration than ETFE 2.4 mm. Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min (0.51×) in 20 mL FEP, BPR 7 bar. Preferred Stage 1 geometry among near-batch Stage 1 candidates. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 0.51× batch; oxidation adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.
5 mL PFA quantity: 2 available; one consumed here, leaving one for other use.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL PFA 1 mm, BPR 7 bar. Short Stage 2 in narrow-bore PFA; no large-bore concern. Both stages substantially below batch. Provides short-time comparison point against C1 and C6. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: Both stages significantly below batch anchors; adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL FEP 1 mm (max 50 °C), BPR 7 bar. FEP temperature ceiling 50 °C is not limiting at 25 °C screen. Functionally identical to C7 in times; differs only in Stage 2 material (FEP vs PFA). Redundant with C7 unless material comparison is intended.
uncertainties: FEP coil max 50 °C limits future temperature exploration in Stage 2.
Both stages below batch; adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04×) in 5 mL ETFE 2.4 mm; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, BPR 7 bar. Near-batch Stage 1 but large-bore throughout; photon penetration concern in both stages. Short Stage 2. Backflow unresolved. All-ETFE design limits photon penetration assessment.
uncertainties: Large bore (2.4 mm) in both stages: photon penetration and gas-liquid distribution uncharacterized.
Stage 2 at 0.25× batch may be insufficient.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, BPR 2.5 bar. Lower BPR increases in-channel gas volume vs C5; may affect slug stability. ETFE large bore Stage 2 concern retained. Provides BPR vs C5 comparison for large-bore Stage 2.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm Stage 2 with BPR 2.5 bar: larger gas void fraction; slug stability uncharacterized.
Stage 1 and Stage 2 both below batch.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04×) in 5 mL ETFE 2.4 mm; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL PFA 1 mm, BPR 7 bar. Near-batch Stage 1 (large bore, photon concern) with short narrow-bore Stage 2. Mixes bore geometries across stages; provides near-batch Stage 1 with short Stage 2 in PFA. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm Stage 1: photon penetration at Re≈0.18 uncharacterized.
Stage 2 at 0.25× batch; oxidation adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL PFA 1 mm, BPR 2.5 bar. Narrow bore both stages; lower BPR than C7. Useful BPR comparison to C7. Both stages well below batch. Functionally overlaps C7 and C10 in screen space.
uncertainties: Both stages below batch; adequacy for both reactions uncharacterized.
Lower BPR increases gas void fraction vs C7.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.
