computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved mitigation proposal (requires chemistry, inventory, and O2-service review before adoption): Install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g., CV-3301, service-verified) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction, protecting Stage 1 from reverse gas intrusion. This valve's cracking pressure concerns the pressure difference across it, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Its maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow behaviour must be confirmed before use.

Unapproved mitigation proposal: A pressure-decoupled arrangement (e.g., intermediate collection and re-pressurisation) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is not a designed or approved element and requires full engineering review.
Reducing gas flow alone does not resolve the unprotected reverse path on the liquid branch, as confirmed by the measured backflow event in the prior experiment and the topology finding.
limitations: Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters: illustrative viscosity (1.0 mPa·s), gas plenum (0.2 mL), MFC required ΔP (1.0 bar), pump response (1.0 s), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), and multiphase resistance multiplier (3.0). These are not laboratory setpoints.
No reversal predicted in the finite simulation windows does not establish safe operation or exclude backflow under real startup, transient, or off-normal conditions.
Reported metric is predicted liquid displacement from the liquid branch at the junction, not oxygen reaching Stage 1 Reactor.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure; steady-state behaviour was only assessed with the hypothetical liquid check valve configuration, which is unassigned and service-unverified.
The CV-3301 check valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve; its maximum pressure rating is unconfirmed.
Isothermal ideal gas model; slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, reaction, and gas-front dynamics are not modelled.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or design is changed by the tool.
The prior experimental gas reverse flow observation (KHU, 15 Sep 2026) used unverified reference conditions and remains unresolved by these simulations.
BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics, and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
Pure O2 use is a gas-source change from the protocol (air); it is unapproved and requires laboratory review before use.

proposed_alternatives: A dedicated check valve (CV-3301 or equivalent) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction is an unapproved proposal: requires engineering review, inventory confirmation, service verification, and oxygen-compatibility assessment before use.
A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., gravity or pressure-controlled transfer) is an unapproved hypothesis requiring separate engineering and chemistry review.

Pure O2 gas supply in place of the batch air atmosphere is an unapproved gas-source change: requires chemist confirmation, oxygen-service review, and materials compatibility assessment before laboratory use.

CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; the valve on the MFC branch does not protect the liquid branch. Branch-specific protection on the liquid line is a separate unapproved item.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, unmeasured parameters (viscosity, compliance, gas plenum, conductance, pump and MFC response times); results are conditional model outputs, not measured evidence or safety certification.

No liquid displacement predicted in entered-profile scenarios does not establish that backflow cannot occur; the unprotected liquid-branch reverse path (st2_mixer → st1_reactor) is an unresolved credible risk confirmed by the KHU qualitative observation.

Candidates 3, 6, and 11 (as-designed, gas-first startup): BPR opening pressure was not reached within the simulated window; steady-state behaviour during full pressurisation is unconfirmed for those as-designed cases.
Predicted quantities are liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches Stage 1 Reactor; actual gas transport through the liquid column is not modelled.
Gas check-valve cracking pressure (1.0 bar) governs pressure difference across that valve; it does not set a minimum system pressure margin above which backflow is precluded.
Isothermal ideal-gas model; no slug, dissolution, capillary, multiphase front, or reaction model included.
Finite scenario window; no lifetime, frequency, or reliability assessment is provided.
Hypothetical liquid-branch check valve is not assigned, not service-verified, and not in the approved inventory; zero leakage assumed is an idealisation.
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating not supplied; suitability at 7 bar or 8 bar system pressures requires laboratory verification before use.
All candidates share the same unresolved reverse-path finding (BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor); reducing gas flow does not close this path.
Acrylonitrile is listed as excluded from RED pump tubing; all candidates correctly assign liquid feed to BLUE pump, but solvent-wetted component compatibility beyond pump tubing should be confirmed.

DrChemistry.justification: Baseline: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42× batch) in 2 mL PFA/UV-150 450 nm; Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min (0.51× batch) in 20 mL FEP/Manual2, BPR 7 bar. Balanced stage ratios. Interpretable anchor for comparison. Backflow unresolved (shared); all other checks pass.
uncertainties: Stage 1 at 100 min (0.42× batch) may be inadequate for Giese reaction; uncharacterized.
Stage 2 apparent tau is inlet/STP index only; liquid exposure much longer but unverified.
Backflow: unprotected reverse path to Stage 1 unresolved.
CV-3301 pressure rating unconfirmed.
O2 service and gas-source change unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 identical to C1 (100 min, 0.42×). Stage 2 same reactor (20 mL FEP) and inlet tau (181.8 min) but BPR 2.5 bar; in-channel gas volume larger (0.028 mL/min vs 0.012 mL/min), potentially different gas-liquid contact. Useful BPR comparison to C1. Backflow unresolved (shared).
uncertainties: Lower BPR may increase gas void fraction; gas-liquid mass transfer and slug stability uncharacterized.
Stage 1 adequacy at 100 min uncharacterized.
Backflow: unprotected reverse path unresolved.
CV-3301 rating unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04× batch) in 5 mL ETFE/UV-150; provides near-batch Stage 1 exposure. Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min (0.51×) in 20 mL FEP, BPR 7 bar. Large-bore ETFE in Stage 1 (2.4 mm ID, Re≈0.18) is laminar; photon penetration depth at 2.4 mm bore unverified. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm bore: photon penetration and mixing at Re≈0.18 uncharacterized in UV-150.
Stage 2 apparent tau 0.51× batch; adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min in 20 mL FEP, BPR 1.5 bar. Lowest BPR of the 20 mL FEP group; highest in-channel gas volume fraction (0.040 mL/min). Useful low-BPR comparison point. Stage 1 adequacy and backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: BPR 1.5 bar: largest gas void fraction among FEP 20 mL candidates; slug flow stability uncharacterized.
Stage 1 at 100 min (0.42×) may be insufficient.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, BPR 7 bar. Shortest apparent Stage 2 index in the set. Stage 2 exposure substantially below batch anchor; adequacy is an open question. ETFE large bore in Stage 2 may affect gas distribution.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 0.25× batch may be insufficient for sulfide oxidation; uncharacterized.
ETFE 2.4 mm bore Stage 2: gas-liquid distribution uncharacterized.
Stage 1 at 0.42× may be insufficient.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04×) in 5 mL PFA 1 mm/UV-150; near-batch Stage 1 in a narrow-bore coil with better photon penetration than ETFE 2.4 mm. Stage 2 tau_inlet=181.8 min (0.51×) in 20 mL FEP, BPR 7 bar. Preferred Stage 1 geometry among near-batch Stage 1 candidates. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 0.51× batch; oxidation adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.
5 mL PFA quantity: 2 available; one consumed here, leaving one for other use.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL PFA 1 mm, BPR 7 bar. Short Stage 2 in narrow-bore PFA; no large-bore concern. Both stages substantially below batch. Provides short-time comparison point against C1 and C6. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: Both stages significantly below batch anchors; adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL FEP 1 mm (max 50 °C), BPR 7 bar. FEP temperature ceiling 50 °C is not limiting at 25 °C screen. Functionally identical to C7 in times; differs only in Stage 2 material (FEP vs PFA). Redundant with C7 unless material comparison is intended.
uncertainties: FEP coil max 50 °C limits future temperature exploration in Stage 2.
Both stages below batch; adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04×) in 5 mL ETFE 2.4 mm; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, BPR 7 bar. Near-batch Stage 1 but large-bore throughout; photon penetration concern in both stages. Short Stage 2. Backflow unresolved. All-ETFE design limits photon penetration assessment.
uncertainties: Large bore (2.4 mm) in both stages: photon penetration and gas-liquid distribution uncharacterized.
Stage 2 at 0.25× batch may be insufficient.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, BPR 2.5 bar. Lower BPR increases in-channel gas volume vs C5; may affect slug stability. ETFE large bore Stage 2 concern retained. Provides BPR vs C5 comparison for large-bore Stage 2.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm Stage 2 with BPR 2.5 bar: larger gas void fraction; slug stability uncharacterized.
Stage 1 and Stage 2 both below batch.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=250 min (1.04×) in 5 mL ETFE 2.4 mm; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL PFA 1 mm, BPR 7 bar. Near-batch Stage 1 (large bore, photon concern) with short narrow-bore Stage 2. Mixes bore geometries across stages; provides near-batch Stage 1 with short Stage 2 in PFA. Backflow unresolved.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm Stage 1: photon penetration at Re≈0.18 uncharacterized.
Stage 2 at 0.25× batch; oxidation adequacy uncharacterized.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 tau=100 min (0.42×) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 tau_inlet=90.9 min (0.25×) in 10 mL PFA 1 mm, BPR 2.5 bar. Narrow bore both stages; lower BPR than C7. Useful BPR comparison to C7. Both stages well below batch. Functionally overlaps C7 and C10 in screen space.
uncertainties: Both stages below batch; adequacy for both reactions uncharacterized.
Lower BPR increases gas void fraction vs C7.
Backflow unresolved; CV-3301 unconfirmed; O2 service unapproved.

DrKinetics.justification: S1: 2 mL PFA, τ_liq=100 min (0.42× batch). S2: 20 mL FEP, τ_inlet=181.8 min (0.50× batch), BPR 7 bar, O2 0.09 sccm, 2.01 equiv. Provides a mid-range S1/S2 combination as a baseline. Backflow and O2-service issues unresolved but not a hard violation absent confirmed occurrence.
uncertainties: S1 liquid τ 0.42× batch; adequacy for Giese completion unproven.
S2 inlet/STP index 0.50× batch; liquid exposure ~1000 min (unconstrained by gas index).
Unprotected liquid reverse path to S1 unresolved across all candidates.

shared_assessment.gas_source_change: Pure O2 replacing batch air is a gas-source change. source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is not explicitly set to true in the schema field, but the intake record (Q-GAS-001) records this as a user-confirmed requirement and the measured-evidence context notes the prior experiment used O2 without design approval, resulting in observed reverse flow. Pure O2 use remains unapproved for oxygen-service purposes across all candidates and must undergo chemist, inventory, and oxygen-service review before laboratory execution.
shared_assessment.reverse_path_finding: All twelve candidates share an unresolved credible risk: BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor. The liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction carries no forward-oriented non-return protection. The CV-3301 check valve is declared only on the MFC (gas) branch; it does not protect the liquid branch. A valve on one branch does not protect a different branch. The KHU qualitative observation (15 Sep 2026) of gas reverse flow is unresolved measured evidence. Reducing gas flow does not close this unprotected reverse path. No simulation result — including the tool's prediction of zero liquid displacement — establishes that backflow cannot occur: the tool uses illustrative unmeasured parameters and a finite scenario window, and its output is predicted liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches or does not reach Stage 1. This finding requires branch-specific engineering review before any candidate is executed.
shared_assessment.physics_tool_status: DrFluidics and DrSafety results are conditional on unmeasured illustrative parameters (viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC ΔP 1.0 bar, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, multiphase resistance multiplier 3.0). No reversal predicted in these finite scenario windows does not establish safety or exclude backflow under real startup, off-normal, or shutdown conditions. Candidates 3, 6, and 11 gas-first startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulated window; steady-state behaviour for those as-designed cases is unconfirmed.
shared_assessment.cv3301_pressure_rating: CV-3301 cracking pressure is 1.0 bar; this concerns the pressure difference across that valve. The maximum pressure rating of CV-3301 is not supplied and must be verified before use at 7 bar or 8 bar system pressures. Cracking pressure is not a pressure rating.
shared_assessment.stage2_temperature: Stage 2 batch temperature is not stage-resolved in the protocol. All candidates assign 25°C; this is unverified. No validated rate correction or yield consequence can be stated.
shared_assessment.stage2_gas_residence_time: Stage 2 Q_gas_sccm and Q_gas_STP values are gas volume at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). The apparent residence-time index V/(Q_liquid + Q_gas_STP) is not a measured liquid residence time or photon exposure index. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake.
shared_assessment.wavelength_note: Protocol specifies 452 nm. Assigned light sources are UV-150/450 nm (Stage 1) and Manual 2/448 nm (Stage 2). These are nearest available; adequacy for catalyst excitation is not established.
shared_assessment.acrylonitrile_pump: Acrylonitrile is excluded from RED pump tubing. All candidates assign liquid feed to BLUE pump; this is consistent with the exclusion constraint.
shared_assessment.no_kinetic_data: Kinetics are uncharacterized for both stages. Stage-hold ratios are exposure indices only. No yield, conversion, or rate superiority can be inferred from any ratio or residence-time comparison. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice; short times are not inherently failures.
shared_assessment.large_bore_ETFE_photon: Candidates using ETFE 5 mL or 10 mL coils (ID 2.4 mm) in Stage 1 or Stage 2 carry an uncharacterized photon penetration uncertainty. The batch protocol used a narrow-bore tube irradiated at close range; 2.4 mm ID reduces surface-to-volume ratio and increases path length. This is an unresolved experimental uncertainty, not a hard violation.
shared_assessment.FEP_temperature: FEP coils (coil_row6, coil_row7) have max temperature 50°C. At the 25°C screen temperature this is not a constraint, but it limits future elevated-temperature exploration at Stage 2 for candidates using those reactors.

required_measurements: Branch-specific non-return protection on the liquid line between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction: verify device identity, service direction, cracking pressure differential, maximum pressure rating, O2 compatibility, and low-flow seating behaviour before execution of any candidate.
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating: must be confirmed independently from cracking pressure specification before use at system pressures up to 7–8 bar.

Chemist and oxygen-service review of pure O2 substitution for the batch air atmosphere: O2 concentration, materials compatibility, MFC service range, and laboratory safety approval required before any candidate is executed.

Gas supply pressure and MFC inlet differential pressure at operating conditions: required to validate model margin estimates; illustrative values (12 bar supply, 1.0 bar ΔP required) are not measured setpoints.
Stage 2 batch temperature: protocol does not resolve a temperature for Stage 2; confirm operating temperature before designing rate or yield expectations.
Startup sequence and pressure traces for Stage 1–Stage 2 connected operation: required to validate or falsify the unresolved backflow risk and simulation predictions.
Photon penetration depth for 2.4 mm ID ETFE coils (Stage 1 in C3, C6 startup comparison; C9, C11): verify irradiance at reaction locus relative to 452 nm protocol lamp at 3 cm distance.
Stage 1 Giese conversion as a function of flow residence time: minimum data point needed to select a Stage 1 reactor for yield-optimised operation.
Stage 2 oxidation completion as a function of flow residence time and O2 equivalent at 7 bar and 2.5 bar: required to distinguish among Stage 2 reactor and BPR options.
Acrylonitrile compatibility and solubility in EtOH:pH 9 buffer at 0.2 M stock concentration: confirm no precipitation or phase separation in the pump and inlet tubing at 0.02 mL/min.

request.task: Select an experiment using objective_policy, evidence and constraints. Do not substitute baseline similarity for the stated priority. Do not invent yield. Compare the selected candidate against at least two other eligible candidates with different stage exposures. Explain why the trade-off meets the priority, what cannot be inferred, and what measurement would change the choice. No forced time increase or decrease. Never choose outside eligible_ids.

scientific_assessment.screening_policy: Fixed exploratory stage-time multipliers relative to explicit batch holds; these are not kinetic predictions.
scientific_assessment.objective: Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage flow process that maximizes the final yield of sulfoxide 4a while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.

objective_policy.objective: Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage flow process that maximizes the final yield of sulfoxide 4a while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.
objective_policy.selection_instruction: Establish an interpretable baseline and compare shorter and longer stage holds.
objective_policy.interpretation_note: Ambiguous or unrecognized wording uses a balanced screen; select a priority explicitly to override.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

selection.objective_alignment: Balanced priority requires an interpretable starting point from which shorter and longer stage holds can be compared. C1 anchors the screen at 0.42× batch (S1) and 0.51× batch (S2), covering sub-batch exposure for both stages simultaneously. This is not the shortest or longest design; it is the mid-range combination that allows yield data from a single run to direct subsequent experiments toward longer S1 (C3, C6) or longer S2 (if both 0.42× and 0.51× prove insufficient), or shorter (C7, C12) if both are already excessive. BPR 7 bar provides the highest O2 pressure head among FEP-20 mL candidates, minimising one source of Stage 2 variability. No yield or conversion can be inferred; adequacy of either stage is uncharacterized.

alternatives.reason_not_selected: S1 at 250 min (1.04× batch) in 5 mL PFA 1 mm provides near-batch Stage 1 exposure and is the preferred near-batch S1 candidate (narrow bore, better photon geometry than ETFE 2.4 mm). However, gas-first as-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR opening pressure within the finite window, leaving full steady-state startup behaviour unconfirmed. Under balanced priority with no prior data, spending the first experiment on a near-batch S1 condition without confirming startup operability is less efficient than C1 as an anchor. If C1 data show Stage 1 conversion is limiting, C6 becomes the priority follow-up.

S1: 100 min (0.42× batch, same as C1); S2: 10 mL PFA 1 mm, τ_inlet=90.9 min (0.25× batch), BPR 7 bar. Provides the short-S2, short-S1 bracketing point. S2 apparent index is the lowest among narrow-bore 7-bar candidates; if oxidation requires closer to batch time, this condition risks insufficient Stage 2 exposure without yielding diagnostic information. C1's longer S2 (181.8 min, 0.51× batch) is more likely to produce detectable product, making C1 more informative as the first experiment. C7 is the recommended short-S2 follow-up after C1.

S1: 5 mL ETFE 2.4 mm, τ_liq=250 min (1.04× batch); S2: 20 mL FEP, τ_inlet=181.8 min, BPR 7 bar. Near-batch S1 in large-bore ETFE; photon penetration at 2.4 mm ID is uncharacterized relative to the batch narrow-tube geometry. Additionally, gas-first as-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR opening pressure (finite window). The combination of uncharacterized photon delivery and unconfirmed startup makes C3 less interpretable as a first experiment than C1 (PFA 1 mm, simpler startup profile). If S1 is rate-limiting, C6 (same τ, narrow bore, confirmed photon geometry) is preferred over C3.

council_answer_assessments.effect: Pure O2 confirmed by chemist (Q-GAS-001); however, this is an unapproved gas-source change relative to the batch air atmosphere and requires oxygen-service review and laboratory safety confirmation before use. The answer sets the gas identity but does not establish approval for oxygen service.

Oxygen introduction at Stage 2 inlet only is implemented in C1 (and all candidates). The unprotected liquid-branch reverse path means this constraint cannot be guaranteed without branch-specific non-return protection; this remains unresolved.

The KHU qualitative backflow observation (15 Sep 2026) is the only measured operability evidence. It directly motivates the unresolved reverse-path finding and confirms that reducing gas flow alone does not resolve the topology risk. It does not quantify backflow rate or conditions.

Stage 1 oxygen exclusion depends on resolving the liquid-branch reverse path before execution. Stage 2 oxygen availability is determined by BPR (7 bar in C1 maximises O2 partial pressure) and inlet equivalents (2.01 equiv); gas-liquid mass transfer is uncharacterized. The hypothesis that Stage 1 sulfide formation limits Stage 2 oxidation cannot be tested until Stage 1 conversion data are available.

answer_effects.note: Equivalent objectives may select the same design. A changed answer does not require an artificial topology change.

chief.justification: Candidate 1 (S1: 2 mL PFA, τ_liq=100 min, 0.42× batch; S2: 20 mL FEP, τ_inlet=181.8 min, 0.51× batch; BPR 7 bar, 2.01 equiv O2, 0.09 sccm) is selected as the interpretable balanced baseline. Under balanced priority with no kinetic data, neither stage should be assumed adequate or inadequate from time ratios alone. C1 provides mid-range exposure in both stages, uses narrow-bore (1 mm) PFA and FEP giving defined photon geometry, and sets the highest system pressure among the 20 mL FEP group (7 bar), maximising dissolved O2 driving force for Stage 2. All shared unresolved issues apply; no hard violations found.

applies_to_all_candidates: Unprotected liquid-branch reverse path: gas introduction junction (Stage 2) connects directly to Stage 1 reactor via the liquid branch with no forward-oriented non-return valve on that branch. The CV-3301 check valve is declared only on the MFC (gas) branch and does not protect the liquid branch. This is an unresolved credible risk (BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor) across all twelve candidates. Reducing gas flow does not close this path. Branch-specific non-return protection on the liquid line must be reviewed before any candidate is executed.

Pure O2 substitution: The protocol specifies air (ambient atmosphere). Use of pure O2 was not approved in the original design; the prior experiment used O2 without design approval and observed reverse flow. Pure O2 use constitutes an unapproved gas-source change requiring chemist confirmation, oxygen-service review, and materials compatibility assessment before laboratory execution.

CV-3301 pressure rating: Cracking pressure (1.0 bar) is not a pressure rating. Maximum pressure rating of CV-3301 is unconfirmed and must be verified before use at 7–8 bar system pressures. The cracking pressure concerns the differential pressure across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure.

Physics tool results: DrFluidics and DrSafety outputs are conditional on illustrative unmeasured parameters (viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC ΔP 1.0 bar, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, multiphase resistance multiplier 3.0). No liquid displacement predicted does not establish safe operation or exclude backflow under real startup, transient, or shutdown conditions. Tool output is predicted liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches or does not reach Stage 1.

Gas residence-time index: Q_gas_sccm and Q_gas_STP values are gas volume at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). The apparent Stage 2 index V/(Q_liquid + Q_gas_STP) is not a measured liquid residence time or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed inlet molar ratios, not measured stoichiometric uptake.
Wavelength: Protocol specifies 452 nm. UV-150/450 nm (Stage 1) and Manual 2/448 nm (Stage 2) are nearest available; photon adequacy for catalyst excitation is not established.
Stage 2 temperature: Not batch-resolved. All candidates assign 25°C; no validated rate correction is available.
Kinetics: Uncharacterized for both stages. No yield, conversion, or rate superiority can be inferred from any hold ratio.
Acrylonitrile: Excluded from RED pump tubing. All candidates assign liquid feed to BLUE pump; consistent with exclusion constraint.

shared_assessment.gas_source_change: Pure O2 replacing batch air is a gas-source change. source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is not explicitly set to true in the schema field, but the intake record (Q-GAS-001) records this as a user-confirmed requirement and the measured-evidence context notes the prior experiment used O2 without design approval, resulting in observed reverse flow. Pure O2 use remains unapproved for oxygen-service purposes across all candidates and must undergo chemist, inventory, and oxygen-service review before laboratory execution.
shared_assessment.reverse_path_finding: All twelve candidates share an unresolved credible risk: BF-REVERSE-PATH:st2_mixer:s3:st1_reactor. The liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction carries no forward-oriented non-return protection. The CV-3301 check valve is declared only on the MFC (gas) branch; it does not protect the liquid branch. A valve on one branch does not protect a different branch. The KHU qualitative observation (15 Sep 2026) of gas reverse flow is unresolved measured evidence. Reducing gas flow does not close this unprotected reverse path. No simulation result — including the tool's prediction of zero liquid displacement — establishes that backflow cannot occur: the tool uses illustrative unmeasured parameters and a finite scenario window, and its output is predicted liquid displacement at the junction, not confirmation that oxygen reaches or does not reach Stage 1. This finding requires branch-specific engineering review before any candidate is executed.
shared_assessment.physics_tool_status: DrFluidics and DrSafety results are conditional on unmeasured illustrative parameters (viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC ΔP 1.0 bar, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, multiphase resistance multiplier 3.0). No reversal predicted in these finite scenario windows does not establish safety or exclude backflow under real startup, off-normal, or shutdown conditions. Candidates 3, 6, and 11 gas-first startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulated window; steady-state behaviour for those as-designed cases is unconfirmed.
shared_assessment.cv3301_pressure_rating: CV-3301 cracking pressure is 1.0 bar; this concerns the pressure difference across that valve. The maximum pressure rating of CV-3301 is not supplied and must be verified before use at 7 bar or 8 bar system pressures. Cracking pressure is not a pressure rating.
shared_assessment.stage2_temperature: Stage 2 batch temperature is not stage-resolved in the protocol. All candidates assign 25°C; this is unverified. No validated rate correction or yield consequence can be stated.
shared_assessment.stage2_gas_residence_time: Stage 2 Q_gas_sccm and Q_gas_STP values are gas volume at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). The apparent residence-time index V/(Q_liquid + Q_gas_STP) is not a measured liquid residence time or photon exposure index. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake.
shared_assessment.wavelength_note: Protocol specifies 452 nm. Assigned light sources are UV-150/450 nm (Stage 1) and Manual 2/448 nm (Stage 2). These are nearest available; adequacy for catalyst excitation is not established.
shared_assessment.acrylonitrile_pump: Acrylonitrile is excluded from RED pump tubing. All candidates assign liquid feed to BLUE pump; this is consistent with the exclusion constraint.
shared_assessment.no_kinetic_data: Kinetics are uncharacterized for both stages. Stage-hold ratios are exposure indices only. No yield, conversion, or rate superiority can be inferred from any ratio or residence-time comparison. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice; short times are not inherently failures.
shared_assessment.large_bore_ETFE_photon: Candidates using ETFE 5 mL or 10 mL coils (ID 2.4 mm) in Stage 1 or Stage 2 carry an uncharacterized photon penetration uncertainty. The batch protocol used a narrow-bore tube irradiated at close range; 2.4 mm ID reduces surface-to-volume ratio and increases path length. This is an unresolved experimental uncertainty, not a hard violation.
shared_assessment.FEP_temperature: FEP coils (coil_row6, coil_row7) have max temperature 50°C. At the 25°C screen temperature this is not a constraint, but it limits future elevated-temperature exploration at Stage 2 for candidates using those reactors.

candidate_justifications.C1: Baseline: S1 2 mL PFA τ_liq=100 min (0.42×), S2 20 mL FEP τ_inlet=181.8 min (0.51×), BPR 7 bar, 2.01 equiv O2. Balanced sub-batch screen; interpretable anchor. No hard violations. All shared uncertainties apply.
candidate_justifications.C2: Identical reactors to C1; BPR reduced to 2.5 bar. In-channel gas volume 0.028 mL/min (vs 0.012 mL/min in C1); higher gas fraction may alter slug behaviour. Lower pressure reduces O2 solubility driving force — effect uncharacterized. Useful BPR comparison. No hard violations.
candidate_justifications.C3: S1 5 mL ETFE ID 2.4 mm τ_liq=250 min (1.04×); S2 20 mL FEP τ_inlet=181.8 min, BPR 7 bar. Only candidate with S1 at or above batch. Gas-first as-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR opening pressure (finite window); steady-state unconfirmed for that case. ETFE 2.4 mm photon penetration uncharacterized. No hard violations; startup operability warrants chemist attention.

Lowest system pressure of all candidates; in-channel gas volume 0.040 mL/min is highest in 20 mL FEP group. O2 solubility driving force lowest here. Useful low-pressure bracket. No hard violations.

ETFE 2.4 mm in S2: photon penetration and gas-liquid distribution uncharacterized. Shortest S2 apparent index. No hard violations; S2 adequacy most uncertain here.

CV-3301 maximum pressure rating: must be confirmed independently from cracking pressure specification before use at system pressures up to 7–8 bar.

Chemist and oxygen-service review of pure O2 substitution for the batch air atmosphere: O2 concentration, materials compatibility, MFC service range, and laboratory safety approval required before any candidate is executed.

Gas supply pressure and MFC inlet differential pressure at operating conditions: required to validate model margin estimates; illustrative values (12 bar supply, 1.0 bar ΔP required) are not measured setpoints.
Stage 2 batch temperature: protocol does not resolve a temperature for Stage 2; confirm operating temperature before designing rate or yield expectations.
Startup sequence and pressure traces for Stage 1–Stage 2 connected operation: required to validate or falsify the unresolved backflow risk and simulation predictions.
Photon penetration depth for 2.4 mm ID ETFE coils (Stage 1 in C3, C6 startup comparison; C9, C11): verify irradiance at reaction locus relative to 452 nm protocol lamp at 3 cm distance.
Stage 1 Giese conversion as a function of flow residence time: minimum data point needed to select a Stage 1 reactor for yield-optimised operation.
Stage 2 oxidation completion as a function of flow residence time and O2 equivalent at 7 bar and 2.5 bar: required to distinguish among Stage 2 reactor and BPR options.
Acrylonitrile compatibility and solubility in EtOH:pH 9 buffer at 0.2 M stock concentration: confirm no precipitation or phase separation in the pump and inlet tubing at 0.02 mL/min.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox cross-coupling reaction utilizes single electron transfer (SET) mechanism with Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photocatalyst (2 mol%) and tBu-TMG base in DMF solvent under 440 nm blue LED irradiation. The optimized flow process operates at 50°C with a 12-minute residence time at 0.83 mL/min flow rate in a segmented flow reactor using FEP tubing with 10 mL reactor volume. Flow conditions achieved 88% yield compared to 81% yield under batch conditions at 30°C, representing an 8.6% improvement in yield. The primary advantage of flow was enabling higher operating temperature (50°C vs 30°C) with superior heat transfer control, while providing predictable scale-up capability to hundreds of mg/h production rates with significantly shorter reaction times.

_analogies.summary: This Csp2-Csp3 cross-coupling reaction employs photoredox/nickel dual catalysis using Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 as the photocatalyst at 2.5 mol% loading with 2,6-lutidine base in THF solvent. The reaction operates at 30°C with blue LED irradiation at 450 nm in a Vapourtec E-series UV-150 flow reactor (10 mL volume) with a 40-minute residence time at 0.25 mL/min flow rate. Flow processing achieved a remarkable 36-fold intensification, reducing reaction time from 24 hours in batch to just 40 minutes while simultaneously improving yield from 60% to 71%. The dramatic improvement stems from the superior light penetration and photon efficiency of the blue LED system compared to the CFL light source used in batch, combined with the optimized irradiation geometry in the dedicated flow photoreactor.

deliberation_log.summary: 12 hardware-bound candidates reviewed; first experiment selected, chemical performance unvalidated.

pre_council_proposal.residence_time_basis: inlet/STP apparent residence time: V_total / (Q_liquid + Q_gas_STP) = 20 mL / (0.50 + 2.24) mL/min = 7.3 min for Stage 2. Stage 1 liquid-only: V/Q = 10/0.50 = 20 min.
pre_council_proposal.light_setup: Stage 1: Vapourtec UV-150 / 450 nm (light_uv150_row10), 24 W, 355 mW/cm², compatible with E-series/R-series, mounted on 10 mL PFA coil (coil_row5). Stage 2: Manual 2 / Blue Strip LED (light_manual2_row13), 448 nm, mounted on 20 mL FEP coil (coil_row7).
pre_council_proposal.deoxygenation_method: Ar sparging of stock solution for ≥15 min before loading; sealed gas-tight reservoir or syringe; no inline degasser available per inventory. CV-3301 check valve between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 O2 T-mixer prevents O2 backflow.

contents: acrylonitrile (0.20 M, 2.0 equiv, molar flow = 0.1000 mmol/min)
streams.solvent: EtOH:pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v), pre-sparged with Ar
streams.reasoning: Chemistry Plan stream_logic: single premixed liquid feed, all Stage 1 components co-dissolved. Protocol fact: 0.1 M substrate, 2.0 equiv acrylonitrile, 0.5 mol% Ir catalyst. Flow rate 0.50 mL/min gives τ = 10 mL / 0.50 = 20 min for Stage 1 (UV-150, 10 mL PFA coil). Pump: Vapourtec R-series (HPLC, compatible with acrylonitrile, avoids RED tubing exclusion). Acrylonitrile excluded from RED tubing per inventory incompatible_pairs.

streams.pump_role: Pure O2 gas feed via MFC introduced at Stage 2 inlet T-mixer
contents: O2 (pure, 100 mol%, 2.0 equiv relative to substrate at inlet/STP, gas_flow_sccm = 2.24 sccm, gas_flow_actual_mL_min = quantity unresolved pending BPR/temperature correction)
streams.solvent: none (gas phase)
streams.reasoning: Chemistry Plan hard constraint: O2 at 2.0 equiv inlet/STP, introduced only at Stage 2. MFC: Bronkhorst FF-C00, max 10 sccm, O2 capable. O2 equiv calc: substrate molar flow = 0.05 mmol/min; 2.0 equiv O2 = 0.10 mmol/min; at STP (22.4 mL/mmol) = 2.24 mL/min STP = 2.24 sccm. Within MFC range (0.01–10 sccm). In-channel actual flow depends on BPR pressure and temperature (25°C); reported as diagnostic only. CV-3301 check valve mandatory between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 T-mixer to prevent O2 backflow.

pre_council_proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (P-713 PEEK, 34 bar rated) at Stage 2 inlet for gas-liquid O2 introduction
pre_council_proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: all Stage 1 reagents co-dissolved, no pre-irradiation incompatibility. O2 introduced exclusively at Stage 2 inlet via T-mixer joining Stage 1 effluent with O2 gas stream to create gas-liquid segmented flow. CV-3301 check valve placed between Stage 1 reactor outlet and Stage 2 T-mixer to block O2 backflow per KHU historical backflow observation.
pre_reactor_steps: Ar sparge of stock solution: Pre-sparge EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) solution containing substrate, acrylonitrile, and Ir catalyst with argon for ≥15 min before loading into sealed reservoir or gas-tight syringe. Inline degasser unavailable per inventory.
Load Stream A into sealed reservoir or gas-tight syringe connected to Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump. Purge tubing lines with degassed solvent under Ar before starting reaction.
Install CV-3301 check valve (1 bar cracking pressure) at outlet of Stage 1 reactor, upstream of Stage 2 T-mixer, to prevent O2 backflow into Stage 1.
post_reactor_steps: BPR (adjustable, 7 bar, bpr_row3 or bpr_row6) installed at system outlet after Stage 2 reactor to maintain back-pressure for gas-liquid flow stability and prevent solvent flash. BPR required per gas-liquid design rules.
Collect product stream in vial under ambient conditions. No quench step specified in batch protocol.
pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: Two-stage photoredox cascade: Stage 1 Giese radical C–C addition (Ar atmosphere, 452 nm, 25°C), Stage 2 aerobic photooxidation to sulfoxide (O2, 452 nm, 25°C). Key design decisions: (1) Single liquid stream A avoids incompatible pairs; acrylonitrile excluded from RED pump tubing → R-series HPLC pump used. (2) Stage 1 reactor: UV-150 450 nm (24 W, 355 mW/cm²) with 10 mL PFA coil (coil_row5), τ₁ = 20 min; this is a screening starting point anchored to Analogy 3 (40 min in UV-150 for similar Ir-photocatalyzed reaction) scaled by improved photon flux and single-liquid feed simplicity — actual optimum requires experimental determination. (3) Stage 2 reactor: Manual 2 Blue Strip LED (448 nm) with 20 mL FEP coil (coil_row7) for O2 gas-liquid segmented flow, τ₂_inlet/STP = 20 mL / (0.50 + 2.24) mL/min = 7.3 min apparent; actual liquid exposure time longer due to gas holdup. UV-150 cannot be shared between stages simultaneously (only 1 UV-150 slot); Manual 2 strip LED (448 nm, ≈452 nm) used for Stage 2. (4) O2 MFC at 2.24 sccm delivers 2.0 equiv O2 at inlet/STP. CV-3301 check valve mandatory between stages. BPR 7 bar at outlet for gas-liquid pressure control. (5) Batch times (240 min Stage 1, 360 min Stage 2) serve as reference, not targets; flow photon flux is ~50× higher per unit volume than batch LEDs. Analogy 1 (30 min vs 24 h batch) and Analogy 3 (40 min vs 24 h batch) demonstrate large time reductions for Ir-photoredox in flow; 20 min Stage 1 / 7.3 min Stage 2 apparent are initial screening coordinates. (6) No BPR inventory item was listed as 'adjustable' with confirmed setpoint; bpr_row3 (adjustable max 8 bar) is selected at 7 bar setpoint for gas-liquid stabilization.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Stage 2 (gas-liquid, primary report): inlet/STP basis = 20 mL / (0.50 + 2.24) = 7.3 min. Stage 1 (liquid-only): 10 mL / 0.50 = 20 min. Analogy 3 (similar Ir-photoredox, UV-150, 10 mL, 40 min) is closest; UV-150 450 nm delivers higher photon flux than batch 2×5W LEDs; 20 min is a downscaled screening starting point consistent with Analogy 3's 40 min for a longer-batch reaction. Calculation estimated 600 min batch-anchored screening but this reflects batch time without photon intensification factor; analogies 1 and 3 show 30–40 min is appropriate for UV-150 Ir-photoredox flow. Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 (same photocatalyst family), 12 min at 0.83 mL/min in 10 mL FEP, 50°C; at 25°C with different substrate, 20 min is reasonable. No kinetic data — screening coordinates only.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Gas-liquid O2 design in Stage 2: O2 equivalents based on inlet/STP MFC flow per universal physics rules. Pressure-corrected in-channel time not reported as primary. Stage 1 is liquid-only so volume/flow basis applies.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: Stage 2 inlet/STP apparent = 7.3 min as primary reporting value for gas-liquid stage.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: Not calculated as primary; requires knowledge of actual BPR pressure, temperature, and gas holdup fraction. Reported as null per rules — diagnostic only.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.50 mL/min liquid (Stream A only). Gives τ₁ = 20 min in 10 mL Stage 1 coil. Analogy 3: 0.25 mL/min in 10 mL = 40 min; we use 0.50 mL/min for 20 min as initial screen. Analogy 2: 0.83 mL/min in 10 mL = 12 min. 0.50 mL/min is within R-series range (0.01–10 mL/min), setting increment 0.01 mL/min. Re = ρvD/μ ≈ (1000 × 0.0106 × 0.001)/0.001 ≈ 10.6, laminar (Re << 2300).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Protocol fact: 25°C, room temperature maintained with cooling fan. No thermal advantage identified. Chemistry Plan Stage 1 and 2 both specify 25°C. UV-150 min temperature is 25°C (compatible). Manual 2 strip LED operates 25–80°C (compatible). FEP max 50°C (compatible at 25°C).
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: BPR required: gas-liquid O2 feed in Stage 2. Chemistry Plan specifies BPR needed. MFC max 9 bar supply; BPR must be below MFC max. BPR 7 bar (bpr_row3 adjustable max 8 bar, set to 7 bar) selected: provides adequate back-pressure to maintain gas-liquid segmented flow, below pump max (R-series 42 bar, E-series 10 bar), below MFC max 9 bar at outlet after Stage 2. CV-3301 cracking pressure 1 bar; BPR 7 bar ensures positive pressure gradient from Stage 1 to collection. EtOH bp 78°C >> 25°C operating, so BPR not needed for solvent boiling prevention, but required for gas-liquid deterministic flow per rules.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coil reactor — both stages. Chemistry Plan specifies coil. Analogies 2 and 3 both use coil/FEP tubing in flow photoreactors. Inventory provides coil reactors compatible with UV-150 and Manual modules.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: Stage 1: PFA (coil_row5, 10 mL, 1 mm ID) — PFA transparent to visible light, compatible with UV-150, Ir catalyst, acrylonitrile, EtOH/buffer. FEP also transparent but max 50°C; PFA preferred for UV-150 platform. Analogy 3 uses FEP; Analogy 2 uses FEP — both acceptable. PFA chosen for Stage 1 to be safe across temperature range. Stage 2: FEP (coil_row7, 20 mL, 1 mm ID) — FEP transparent for photocatalysis at 448 nm, rated to 50°C (>25°C operating), 34 bar (>7 bar BPR). Manual 2 strip LED used with FEP coil for Stage 2. Photochem rule: FEP/PFA preferred for visible light transparency.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID — from inventory stock coils (coil_row5, coil_row7). Photochem rule: 0.5–2.0 mm recommended for uniform irradiation. 1 mm gives good light penetration for 450 nm. Analogies 1 (2 mm quartz), 2 (FEP unspecified), 3 (UV-150 unspecified ID, inventory standard 1 mm). Chemistry Plan calculation used 1.6 mm for large-scale pressure drop — not applicable at 10/20 mL inventory scale at 0.50 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Stage 1: 10 mL (coil_row5, PFA, 1 mm ID) — matches UV-150 max reactor volume of 10 mL. Analogy 3: 10 mL UV-150 coil, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min; we use 0.50 mL/min giving 20 min. Analogy 2: 10 mL FEP, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min. Stage 2: 20 mL (coil_row7, FEP, 1 mm ID) — largest available coil for Manual 2 module (max 20 mL), provides τ₂_inlet/STP = 7.3 min with gas-liquid feed. Total system reactor volume: 10 + 20 = 30 mL. Primary reported reactor_volume_mL = 10 mL (Stage 1 UV-150 coil).
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Stage 1: UV-150 450 nm (light_uv150_row10, 24 W, 355 mW/cm²) — closest available to protocol 452 nm (2 nm difference, acceptable). Compatible with R-series pump platform and PFA coil ≤10 mL. Analogy 3 uses UV-150 450 nm exactly. Stage 2: Manual 2 Blue Strip LED (light_manual2_row13, 448 nm) — only one UV-150 module available (shared resource), cannot use UV-150 for both stages simultaneously. Manual 2 at 448 nm is within 4 nm of 452 nm target, acceptable for Ir MLCT absorption tail. Manual 2 max reactor volume 20 mL (compatible with coil_row7). Chemistry Plan notes this hardware constraint explicitly.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: Protocol fact: 452 nm. Inventory: UV-150/450 nm (light_uv150_row10) used for Stage 1 (2 nm deviation). Manual 2 Blue Strip LED (448 nm, light_manual2_row13) used for Stage 2 (4 nm deviation). Both within absorption band of [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 MLCT tail (~380–460 nm). Recommended_wavelength_nm from Chemistry Plan = 452 nm.
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Chemistry Plan: Ar sparge before loading (no inline degasser available per inventory). Gas-tight sealed reservoir or syringe. CV-3301 check valve between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 T-mixer. KHU historical backflow observation: at 0.02 mL/min liquid + 0.43 mL/min O2, reverse flow observed; check valve is mandatory mitigation. Stage 1 liquid flow 0.50 mL/min >> 0.02 mL/min historical backflow condition — improved margin, but check valve remains required.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Protocol fact: 0.1 M substrate (limiting). Analogy 2: 0.05 M (lower); Analogy 1: unspecified. We maintain 0.1 M per protocol. Acrylonitrile 0.2 M (2.0 equiv), Ir catalyst 0.0005 M (0.5 mol%). No concentration adjustment made.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: P-713 PEEK T-mixer (34 bar rated) at Stage 2 inlet for O2 gas-liquid introduction. PEEK inert to EtOH/buffer/O2. T-mixer creates segmented gas-liquid flow in 1 mm ID tubing for enhanced mass transfer. Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning cites T-mixer for gas-liquid junction.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_equipment: bpr_row3 (adjustable BPR max 8 bar) set to 7 bar. Fixed BPR 7 bar (bpr_row6) is alternative. Adjustable preferred for screening flexibility. Must be below MFC max 9 bar and below pump max pressure.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: photoredox radical addition + oxidation, fac-[Ir(ppy)3], MiChS photoreactor, 2 mm quartz, 2.7 mL, 30 min residence, 0.09 mL/min, 425 nm — similar Ir-photoredox mechanism, different catalyst and reactor; supports short residence times (30 min) vs 24 h batch; adjusted: our UV-150 with 10 mL coil and different Ir catalyst, use 20 min as starting screen (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling, FEP 10 mL, 12 min at 0.83 mL/min, 440 nm, 50°C, 34 W — same photocatalyst family (dF(CF3)ppy ligand), different coupling type and temperature; adjusted: at 25°C use longer 20 min, 0.50 mL/min in 10 mL PFA UV-150 coil (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

Analogy 3: Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 photoredox/Ni dual catalysis, Vapourtec E-series UV-150, 10 mL, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm, 30°C — closest match: same UV-150 reactor, same 450 nm wavelength, same Ir catalyst class; key difference: dual catalysis vs single photocatalyst; adjusted: use 0.50 mL/min (20 min) as more aggressive screen since single-catalyst radical addition may be faster than dual-catalysis cross-coupling (DOI unresolved from analogy data)

council_physics_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

responses.question: Please provide or confirm the batch reaction protocol, including substrate, product, solvent, concentration, scale, reagents, equivalents, catalyst/additives, gas atmosphere, temperature, time, irradiation/light source if any, and reported yield.
responses.answer:
Step 1: Giese reaction
A re-sealable pressure tube (13 × 100 mm) equipped with a magnetic stir bar was charged with (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv), acrylonitrile (2, 0.4 mmol, 2.0 equiv), and [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.001 mmol, 0.5 mol %) under an argon atmosphere. A degassed solvent mixture (2.0 mL, 0.1 M with respect to 1) of EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1, v/v) was added, and the resulting light greenish-yellow mixture, under vigorous magnetic stirring, was positioned 3 cm from a pair of 5 W blue LEDs (λmax = 452 nm) and irradiated at room temperature (25 °C, maintained with a cooling fan to counteract heating from the LEDs) for 4 h 

Step 2: Oxidation reaction
After 4 h, the cap of the tube was removed to expose the reaction mixture to ambient air, providing atmospheric oxygen as the terminal oxidant, and stirring was continued under otherwise identical irradiation conditions for an additional 6 h.

A degassed solvent mixture (2.0 mL, 0.1 M with respect to 1) of EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1, v/v) was added, and the resulting light greenish-yellow mixture, under vigorous magnetic stirring, was positioned 3 cm from a pair of 5 W blue LEDs (λmax = 452 nm) and irradiated at room temperature (25 °C, maintained with a cooling fan to counteract heating from the LEDs) for 4 h

After 4 h, the cap of the tube was removed to expose the reaction mixture to ambient air, providing atmospheric oxygen as the terminal oxidant, and stirring was continued under otherwise identical irradiation conditions for an additional 6 h.

responses.question: Do you have chemical or engineering hypotheses the agent should consider? Examples: oxygen mass-transfer limitation, photon limitation, slow kinetics, degradation, gas-liquid ratio, residence-time sensitivity, or light intensity importance.
responses.answer: Stage 1 performance may depend on effective oxygen exclusion and photon delivery. Incomplete sulfide formation will limit the material available for subsequent oxidation. Stage 2 may depend on oxygen availability and gas–liquid transport. Use the batch reaction time as a reference rather than a fixed target, and determine the residence time based on flow performance. Balance photon delivery, oxygen feed, pressure, and stage-specific residence times based on the final sulfoxide yield and selectivity.

canonical_explanation:
### Final Executable Design
- **Residence time:** 281.818 min
- **Inlet/STP apparent residence time:** 281.818 min
- **In-channel apparent residence time:** 716.865 min
- **Total liquid flow:** 0.02 mL/min
- **Reactor volume:** 22 mL
- **Temperature:** 25 deg C
- **BPR:** 7 bar
- **Concentration:** 0.1 M
- **Residence-time basis:** sum of per-stage inlet/STP apparent residence time
- **Assigned equipment:** Vapourtec E-series / BLUE pump tubing, PFA coil 2 mL / ID 1 mm, Vapourtec UV-150 / 450 nm, Bronkhorst FLEXI-FLOW Compact FF-C00, CV-3301, P-713 T-mixer, FEP coil 20 mL / ID 1 mm, Manual 2 / Blue Strip LED, BPR max 8 bar, PFA coil 2 mL / ID 1 mm flow path, FEP coil 10 mL / ID 1 mm flow path

limitations: No kinetic data exist for either stage; stage-hold ratios are exposure indices only, not conversion or yield predictors.
The unprotected liquid-branch reverse path is unresolved across all candidates; no candidate can be executed safely until branch-specific non-return protection is reviewed.
Pure O2 is unapproved as a gas source; chemist confirmation, O2-service review, and materials compatibility assessment are required before execution.
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating is unconfirmed; cracking pressure (1.0 bar) is not a pressure rating.
Physics tool (DrFluidics/DrSafety) results are conditional on illustrative unmeasured parameters; no reversal predicted does not establish safe operation.

Stage 2 inlet/STP apparent residence time (181.8 min) is not a measured liquid exposure; liquid τ in Stage 2 is 1000 min (unconstrained by gas index) and actual photon exposure time is also uncharacterized.
Stage 2 temperature is not batch-resolved; 25°C assignment is unverified.
Wavelength mismatch (450/448 nm vs 452 nm target) is unconfirmed as adequate for catalyst excitation.
FEP coil (Stage 2) max temperature 50°C limits future elevated-temperature Stage 2 exploration.
Candidates 3, 6, and 11 as-designed gas-first startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure; startup operability for those designs is unconfirmed.

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 30 mL final-volume basis, charge (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane: 3 mmol (0.1 M final); [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6: 0.015 mmol (0.0005 M final); acrylonitrile: 6 mmol (0.2 M final); add EtOH:pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v), pre-sparged with Ar to 30 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation.
Prepare Stream B: connect O2 to the assigned MFC at 0.09 mL/min at STP on the declared STP basis (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar; 22.414 L/mol); no liquid stock is prepared.
Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 7 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.
Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.
Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints. Admit gas only after liquid flow, temperature, pressure, purge, and vent checks are stable.
Run for at least three canonical residence-time intervals (845 min) before product collection and document pressure, temperature, and flow stability.

operating_procedure.instruction: After steady state, collect product for at least one canonical residence-time interval (282 min); record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.
